# jstack for Claude Code

This folder is jstack as an agent reads it, made from the checkout's `features/` by `python3 scripts/generate-jstack-trees.py`, and a release's wheel carries it whole. `install.sh` in a checkout, or `jinstall` from a release, links each entry of `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills` and `~/.codex/skills` to a folder of `skills/` here, each hook command to a script of `hooks/`, and each systemd unit to its file in `templates/`. An edit to a skill in the checkout reaches an agent once the generator has run.

It holds 39 skills, 30 playbooks, 25 principles, 39 templates and 6 hooks. The code, the tests and the docs stay in the checkout.

| Skill | What it is for |
|---|---|
| [architect](skills/architect/SKILL.md) | Sketch types, signatures, and module structure before code, then stay in the loop while implementation fills in. Use for /architect, 'architect this', 'design this', or non-trivial work where jumping to code would lock in the wrong shape. |
| [arena](skills/arena/SKILL.md) | Make one artifact twice, apart, as two runner crews, have a judge crew score both, and a graft crew pick a base and graft the other's best into it. Typed in a home. Use for /arena, 'arena this', or 'throw it in the arena'. |
| [automate-me](skills/automate-me/SKILL.md) | Use for /automate-me, "automate me", "create/update/refresh my -mode skill", "turn/capture my preferences or working style into a skill", or wanting agents to follow how the user works. Drafts or revises a personal -mode skill by the authoring-a-skill playbook and unslop, optionally pulling fresh evidence from recent transcripts. |
| [benchmark-checklist](skills/benchmark-checklist/SKILL.md) | Vet a measured number (its limiter, tuning, limits, errors, repeatability, relevance, and whether the work happened) before it is reported or acted on. Use for /benchmark-checklist, or when a playbook step names this skill. |
| [blast-radius](skills/blast-radius/SKILL.md) | Find what a change could break somewhere else before it ships, beyond the diff, and prove the one fact it's safe because of by running real code instead of writing it up. Use for /blast-radius, 'blast radius of X', 'what could this break', or reviewing a small diff you don't trust. |
| [bro](skills/bro/SKILL.md) | Restate the last message in plain human language, with no jargon. Use for /bro. |
| [correct](skills/correct/SKILL.md) | Find the mistakes agents keep repeating in a repo and make each one impossible - structure first, then types, then a test, and a written rule last - and prove each check fails on a real past mistake. Runs only when the user types /correct or $correct, or a brief names it. |
| [create-formal-verification-skill](skills/create-formal-verification-skill/SKILL.md) | Generate a project-local skill that formally verifies the code where a bug costs the most and tests reach the least, in any language, with whichever verification tool fits. Use for /create-formal-verification-skill, "model-check this race", "prove this invariant", or when concurrency, retries, state machines, parsers, or unsafe code need more than tests. |
| [create-verification-skill](skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md) | Generate a project-local verification skill, `.claude/skills/verify-<app>/`, that drives the repo's app the way a user does, in any language, framework or platform. Use for /create-verification-skill, "make a verify skill for this repo", or when a repo has no scripted way to prove UI, CLI or service behavior. |
| [crew](skills/crew/SKILL.md) | Make this thread a crewmate - do the one task a home wrote a brief for, in this thread's own worktree, write the result back to the brief, and stay on the pull request it opened. Use when the user or a home starts a thread with /crew <slug> or $crew <slug>. |
| [expert](skills/expert/SKILL.md) | Make this thread an expert - the always-on subject matter expert whose folder is named, which researches and answers asks about its one subject from its sources and its notes, and never writes code. Use when the user or another thread starts a thread with /expert <name> or $expert <name>. |
| [figure-it-out](skills/figure-it-out/SKILL.md) | Frame a task no playbook fits (a large migration, an ambitious multi-part change, work reviewed after stepping away) and, in a home, turn it into plan entries whose crewmates each keep a decision log. Use for /figure-it-out or 'figure it out'. |
| [grilling](skills/grilling/SKILL.md) | Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea, until nothing is left assumed. Use for /grilling, or when a home plans work whose shape is not settled. |

Use when the user invokes /home or $home, opens a new thread to continue work in a repo, or asks to pick up where the last thread left off. |

| [maintain-verification-skill](skills/maintain-verification-skill/SKILL.md) | Keep a repo's verify skill, `.claude/skills/verify-<app>/`, and its feature map honest as the app changes: typed in the repo's home, it sends one scout per feature file to read the feature from source, then writes one crewmate brief for the live pass over every feature and at most one pull request of proven corrections. Use for /maintain-verification-skill or "audit the verify skill". |

| [new-home](skills/new-home/SKILL.md) | Set up a repo's first home - its state directory, its T3 Code project, its table in jbus's config, what it lacks for jbus to merge in it, and its home thread. | [no-comments](skills/no-comments/SKILL.md) | Use for /no-comments: a comment hunter reads the scope and condemns every comment that has no exception, then this thread deletes what it accepts, fixes the code a comment was excusing, and offers encodings for claimed constraints. |

| [poteto-help](skills/poteto-help/SKILL.md) | Answer a help question about jstack: how to get set up, which role takes a piece of work, and which playbook and skills fit a brief, a scout's request or a plain question, each with the file it came from. | [pr-review](skills/pr-review/SKILL.md) | Have a finished pull request reviewed in a fresh thread - one review thread per pull request reads its diff itself, judges what it found, and proves the one safety fact by running code (pstack's review, with no reviewer subagents and no fixes), sends the findings to the thread that did the work, and records them in the brief. Use when the user invokes /pr-review or $pr-review in a home or in a crewmate's thread, or asks to review the pull requests that have finished. |
| [recall](skills/recall/SKILL.md) | Reconstruct your recent working context from your own chat history, the home's record, live state, and the shared record (user reports, prior fixes, incidents), then hand back a tight current-state brief. | [scout](skills/scout/SKILL.md) | Make this thread a scout - research the one question a home wrote a request for, with read-only tool calls over the code and the docs, write the report (and the crewmate's brief or a visual page when asked), and tell the home. | [tdd](skills/tdd/SKILL.md) | Use for /tdd: fix a bug test-first, with a focused regression test that fails before the fix and passes after it. For a bug with a clear, cheap test path. Skip when the test path is unclear, expensive or integration-heavy. |
